title: P26: 16 attention heads of 16 dims (8 ALiBi slopes 1/2..1/256 + 8 NoPE) instead of 8 of 32 (4 + 4) in all six Peri-LN blocks, on the 115-fable hybrid Lean incumbent
description: P26 on the 115-fable hybrid ALiBi/NoPE incumbent: N_HEAD 8 -> 16 at fixed d_model 256, so every block has 8 ALiBi heads (standard 8-head slope set 1/2..1/256, a finer locality ladder than 115's 1/4..1/256) and 8 content-only NoPE heads of 16 dims; matrix shapes, compute and the 4,800,000 parameters are unchanged. The 4+4 head split was the largest Lean-protocol gain, and doubling both channel types should hand expert iteration a model with more independent citation lookups per proof line at the same cost.
hypothesis: A Lean proof line often cites several premises (theorem hypotheses and earlier n_k lines) and each head's softmax retrieves about one of them, so 4 content heads per block bottleneck retrieval, while 16-dim keys are still plenty to match a 107-token vocabulary with offset names. More, narrower heads give more simultaneous retrieval channels plus a finer span of locality scales, which should show up as a better round-1 RL start (more targets solved, no more parse failures) at unchanged parameters and throughput.
expected_delta: -35 to +35 dev solves >= 7 vs 115-fable's 631.33 (central +5); round-1 targets solved 650-780 (115: 718/756/691), round-1 parse failures 15-30% (115: 25/22/18%); pretraining steps 4,000-4,350 (115: 4204/4218/4263; dim-16 attention may cost a few %), final val loss 0.079-0.086 (115: 0.0826/0.0806/0.0792); totals 1,500-1,800 s under the 2,400 s cap. Failure mode: 16-dim heads too low-rank for name matching under the shift augmentation, seen as higher val loss and a weaker round 1

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks (LayerNorm on each branch output as well as its input) and hybrid attention heads: CHANGED head count, 16 heads of 16 dims, ALiBi on 8 heads and no positional signal on the other 8 (P26 on the P34 x P32 hybrid)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope, CHANGED slope table for 16 heads: no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/8) = 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32, 1/64, 1/128, 1/256 for heads 1..8 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 8 heads) and 0 for heads 9..16 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: CHANGED vs 115-fable: only N_HEAD 8 -> 16 (head dim 32 -> 16) and, through N_ALIBI = N_HEAD // 2 = 8, the slope table (standard 8-head set 1/2..1/256 then 8 zeros; 115 used 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 then 4 zeros). qkv (768,256), proj, fc1, fc2, embeddings, readout, all LayerNorms, depth, GELU, init, optimizer and schedule are byte-identical, so n_params is unchanged. Each block's q/k/v are viewed as (B, T, 3, 16, 16) instead of (B, T, 3, 8, 32); SDPA runs 16 heads of dim 16 with the same additive mask
arch.n_params_detail: identical to 115-fable: 4,800,000 (vocab 107); head count changes no tensor shape; slopes buffer (1,16,1,1) is not a parameter
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 16) from this pretrain.py (its ALIBI_SLOPES = (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32, 1/64, 1/128, 1/256, 0 x 8)), replace blocks with PeriLNBlock(256, 16) as in pretrain.py, then load state (same keys and shapes as 115). Loading these weights into 115's 8-head model gives a different function. The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval
arch.kv_cache: code unchanged from 115 (caches[0] holds key positions; slope-0 heads get a zero bias plus the -inf mask); cache tensors become (B, 16, max, 16) via PeriLNBlock's self.h and D // self.h. No local cached-vs-full check this session: the local fork checkout is not at the pinned commit; the head count enters only through the fork's Block(d, h) and the view/permute in PeriLNBlock.attn

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 115-fable: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V by its (3D, D) shape, which head count does not change; proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, CHANGED: + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: unchanged from 115-fable: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V by its (3D, D) shape, which head count does not change; proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1
